title: Late and duplicate events: dedupe first, then decide if the bucket is still open
caption: The watermark says when a bucket is final; allowed lateness says how long a final bucket may still be corrected.

steps.text: Brokers and clients retry, so check the event id against a short dedup window before counting (see idempotency).
Bucket by event time, not arrival time: a click from 12:00:59 that arrives at 12:01:30 belongs to 12:00.
The bucket's window hasn't been closed by the watermark yet (say end + 2 min): just add to it.
Already emitted but within the allowed lateness: upsert the row. The dashboard number changes slightly.
Too late: send it to a correction log, and let the nightly batch job rebuild that bucket from the raw events.

scenarios.name: Late but allowed
scenarios.summary: A click from 12:00:59 arrives at 12:03:30, after the watermark closed 12:00, but within the allowed lateness: the emitted row is upserted and the dashboard number ticks up.

steps.text: Its event time puts it in the 12:00 bucket.
The watermark has already passed 12:00's end (+2 min), so that row was emitted.
It's within the allowed lateness (say 1 hour): upsert the final row.

scenarios.name: Hours late
scenarios.summary: A phone reconnects six hours later with yesterday's clicks: past the allowed lateness, so they go to the correction log and the nightly batch rebuilds those buckets from raw.

steps.text: A batch of events arrives with event times six hours ago.
Their buckets were closed by the watermark long ago.
Beyond the allowed lateness: the stream won't reopen state that old.
The nightly job recounts those buckets from the raw log and overwrites them.

scenarios.name: Duplicate delivery
scenarios.summary: A broker retry resends an event that was already counted: its id is still in the dedup window, so it's dropped before it touches any bucket.

steps.text: The same click arrives a second time after a producer retry.
Its id is in the dedup window, so it's dropped. Counting it would inflate the bill.

scenarios.name: Risk: lateness too tight
scenarios.summary: Set the watermark and allowed lateness below the real delay of mobile traffic and many events land in the correction log: live numbers undercount until the nightly rebuild.

steps.text: Mobile clients batch clicks and send them minutes later.
With a tight watermark, most of them miss their open bucket.
With little allowed lateness, they skip the upsert and pile into the correction log.
Mitigation: measure the arrival-delay distribution and set lateness above its p99; trade a later 'final' number for a correct one.
